newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam industry output up 13.5 pct by September.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam industry output up 13.5 pct by September.

text.p: Vietnam's industrial output climbed 13.5 percent in the first nine months of this year from the same period in 1995, but the pace of growth has continued to slow, the Government Statistics Office said on Wednesday.
Statistics showed output from the state sector rose by 12.0 percent, from the non-state sector by 12.9 percent and from industry with foreign investment by 18.4 percent.
The 13.5 percent overall rise compared with 14.3 percent recorded in the same period last year.
The office said in a statement that output from state businesses was being hampered by poor technology, a lack of capital, and competition from cheap goods smuggled into Vietnam from abroad.
It also cited slower production increases in the coal, cement, paper, and beer industries as contributing factors.
Output from the oil industry remained static at 11.5 percent.
Despite the figures the office said industrial output for 1996 as a whole was expected to reach 14 percent, on par with the level reported for 1995.
Vietnam's ruling Communist Party announced in a five-year policy blueprint issued in June that state sector industry should play a leading role in the country's economy.
At present the sector accounts for about 40 percent of Gross Domestic Product, but Hanoi has indicated it wishes to see the level substantially increased.
